name: Thermal Signature Inverter TSI-2 'Cold Case'
description: The TSI-2 is a directed energy weapon that projects a focused beam of concentrated Peltier-effect thermal extraction — colloquially described as 'a heat vacuum' — that does not freeze its target in any conventional sense but instead induces rapid, extreme localized hypothermia by stripping thermal energy from the impact zone faster than biological tissue can compensate. At full power against a human torso, the effect produces a roughly 15-centimeter diameter zone of flash-cooled tissue that seizes muscle fibers, fractures capillary walls, and causes immediate motor failure in the affected area. The surrounding tissue remains at body temperature; only the targeted zone is affected, which creates a wound pattern unlike anything produced by conventional weapons.
specifications:
form factor: Compact carbine, 520mm length, distinctive matte-white housing with heat-sink ribbing along barrel
effective range: Up to 35 meters at full effect; partial effect to 50 meters
power source: Liquid-nitrogen-assisted thermoelectric cell, 8 full-power shots or 20 partial shots
weight: 2.2 kg
beam diameter at target: 12–18 cm depending on range
effect onset: Immediate on contact
cooldown between shots: 6 seconds
cell replacement time: 8 seconds
tactical_use: The Cold Case is primarily used for incapacitation rather than killing — a hit to a limb renders it non-functional for 20–40 minutes as tissue gradually rewarms. Corporate security teams use it for detaining high-value targets who need to be taken alive. Bounty contractors favor it because a torso hit is incapacitating but survivable if medical attention arrives within roughly fifteen minutes, giving them a live delivery option. Against heavily armored targets, the TSI-2 is less effective as armor insulates against thermal extraction — it is specifically optimized for lightly armored, highly augmented targets whose cybernetic components are disrupted by the temperature differential.
cultural_context: TESSERA CORPONATION markets the TSI-2 aggressively as a 'humane compliance solution,' and there is a glossy corporate legitimacy to the weapon that other entries in this arsenal lack. Licensed security firms display it visibly as a statement of institutional restraint — 'we have the option not to kill you.' On the street, this reputation is regarded with deep suspicion. Operators know that a Cold Case hit to the torso is survivable only with prompt care, and corporate security is not always motivated to provide that care promptly. The weapon's clean white aesthetic and the bloodless nature of its wounds have made it a favorite in corporate propaganda depicting 'responsible force.'
known_users: Certain police auxiliary units in corporate-administered districts
story_hooks: A bounty contractor delivers a target alive but the target dies of complications from Cold Case exposure two hours later — was it negligence, or did someone slow-walk the medical response intentionally?

A stolen shipment of TSI-2 units has appeared on the black market with the licensing chips removed — someone is planning something that requires the appearance of institutional legitimacy without the paper trail.
A character is hit by a Cold Case round in a situation where medical help is hours away — do they find a solution, or does the clock run out?

TESSERA's 'humane compliance' marketing is being used in a legal case to argue that a security team acted appropriately — but a street medic's testimony about the actual wound progression tells a different story.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular carbine with a distinctly medical aesthetic — all matte-white polymer and precision engineering. The barrel is noticeably thicker than conventional weapons, wrapped in prominent horizontal heat-sink ribbing that makes it look like a piece of clinical equipment rather than a gun. The overall silhouette is compact and forward-heavy, with a pronounced grip angle suggesting precision over spray-and-pray.
physical_description.dimensions: 520mm length overall; barrel 280mm; 85mm width across heat-sink fins; 55mm grip diameter
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced — 2.2 kg feels substantial in hand but never unwieldy, weight distributed toward the barrel assembly where the Peltier chambers sit. The grip sits lower relative to the bore axis, demanding careful control but rewarding it with predictable recoil characteristics.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer composite with embedded aluminum heat-sink framework; barrel assembly houses stainless steel Peltier chamber housings; titanium alloy breech block
physical_description.finish: Matte white with brushed aluminum accents on heat-sink ribbing; anti-glare coating gives it a faintly clinical sheen rather than tactical matte-black. Micro-texturing across major surfaces to reduce fingerprints and thermal signature reflection.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: pharmaceutical white (RAL 9016); accents: gunmetal gray on ribbed heat-sink fins and breech assembly; cryogenic-blue LED indicator strips along the receiver
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer with diamond-pattern surface treatment for secure hold even when wet or contaminated; slight cooling to the touch due to passive heat dissipation through the grip frame. Ergonomic contours favor trigger-finger precision.
distinctive_features: Asymmetrical heat-sink ribbing running the full length of barrel — each fin precision-milled for thermal efficiency
Cryo-blue LED status indicators clustered near the power cell housing (visible on starboard side): charge level, cooldown timer, thermal equilibrium status
Recessed liquid-nitrogen cell port with quick-disconnect coupling on the frame — designed for rapid 8-second swaps
Transparent polycarbonate coolant circulation window running along the upper receiver, showing dark fluid cycling through micro-channels
Precision optics mounting rail with integrated rangefinder interface window
Discharge orifice with six small radiator fins surrounding muzzle opening — appears more like a precision medical instrument than a weapon aperture
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TESSERA CORPORATION logo stamped in matte inlay on starboard receiver; TSI-2 'COLD CASE' designation below; serial plate (brushed stainless) on lower frame; safety warnings in three languages micro-etched on grip frame; cryogenic handling symbols on cell housing
physical_description.condition_typical: When field-used, accumulated frost residue collects around the discharge orifice and heat-sink fins despite thermal insulation — a thin, persistent rime of frozen atmospheric moisture. Handled units show fingerprint oils and microscopic coolant seepage staining around the cell port. Licensed corporate units are meticulously maintained with NO visible wear; unlicensed or heavily-used examples develop scratching on the white finish and discoloration around thermal vents.
